claim: When the user storage accepts the new recovery codes, an existing Keycloak-stored recovery-codes credential is never removed, so old codes stay valid after the user regenerates them.

When the credential comes from user storage and all codes are used, the authenticator calls removeStoredCredentialById with the storage credential's id against Keycloak's own store; the id is null for models built with createFromValues, so JPA em.find(null) throws, and the storage-owned credential is never removed.

A user-storage provider that supports and validates recovery codes but does not override CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials (default Stream.empty()) makes credentialModelOpt.get() throw NoSuchElementException, so the recovery-code login page fails with a 500.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Login page depends on an undocumented getCredentials() contract for user-storage providers

**Severity:** MEDIUM -- the recovery-code login page crashes for storage providers that implement only the validate/update methods

### The Problem
```java
Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);
RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel recoveryCodeCredentialModel =
        RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get());
this.codeNumber = recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get().getNumber();
```
With this PR, a storage provider can store recovery codes through `updateCredential` and report them through `isConfiguredFor`/`isValid`. Rendering the login page, however, also needs the provider to override `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials`. It must return a `CredentialModel` in Keycloak's internal JSON format: `RecoveryAuthnCodesSecretData` with hashed codes and numbers.

### Theory / Proof
- `CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials` defaults to `Stream.empty()` (server-spi/.../CredentialInputUpdater.java:50-52).
- `UserCredentialManager.isConfiguredFor` returns CONFIGURED from the storage validator alone (UserCredentialManager.java:250-258), so the authenticator is offered and `createLoginRecoveryAuthnCode` builds this bean.
- `getCredential` then finds nothing in either the federated stream or local storage, and `Optional.get()` throws `NoSuchElementException`.
- If the provider returns a credential in any other format (for example the raw JSON list it received in `updateCredential`), `createFromCredentialModel` throws `RuntimeException` while parsing.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The only provider in the PR (the testsuite provider) overrides `getCredentials` and rebuilds the internal model with `createFromValues`, so the test passes. A third-party provider written against the SPI, which only exposes `supportsCredentialType`/`updateCredential`/`isValid`, gets a 500 on the recovery-code login page. Nothing in the API or its Javadoc tells implementers this is required.

### Recommendation
Handle a missing credential without crashing, and document the contract on `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` or the SPI:
```java
this.codeNumber = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)
        .map(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel::createFromCredentialModel)
        .flatMap(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel::getNextRecoveryAuthnCode)
        .map(RecoveryAuthnCodeRepresentation::getNumber)
        .orElse(-1); // template can then omit the "code number" hint
```

claim: The reference storage provider accepts any stored code on every attempt and never consumes it, so recovery codes are reusable; the login page asks for code #1 while any code is accepted, and the new test does not check one-time use.
Only the raw code list is passed to the user storage; the user label and generatedAt timestamp from the required-action form are dropped for storage-backed credentials.

## [GAP ANALYSIS] User label and creation time are lost when codes are stored in user storage

**Severity:** LOW -- metadata shown in the account console is lost for storage-backed recovery codes

### The Problem
```java
UserCredentialModel recoveryCodesCredential = new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson);
```
`credentialModel` carries `userLabel` (`FIELD_USER_LABEL_HIDDEN`) and `createdDate` (`generatedAt`). Only the code list reaches `updateCredential`, so the storage provider has no way to keep them. The reference provider sets `createdDate = Time.currentTimeMillis()` and returns `getUserLabel()` as null.

### Theory / Proof
The local path passes the full `credentialModel` to `createCredential`, which keeps both fields. `CredentialInput` has no label field, so this only works if the label goes with the value some other way.

### Recommendation
Pass the complete `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` (with plaintext codes) as the input, or serialize it into the challenge response, e.g. `{"codes":[...],"label":...,"createdDate":...}`. That way storage providers can keep the metadata the local path already keeps.
